subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or a documented decision that coarse scopes are the intended core boundary?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions, protected backup contents, and whether the feature belongs in core affects recovery guarantees and user data safety, so automation should not choose the policy while a linked PR is already under review.

options.title: Review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, live proof, protected-path semantics, and restore-critical defaults.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Prove current or replacement backup code completes or fails clearly on large state dirs, then track smart/custom exclusions under the broader backup-exclude issue.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document native backup limits and point users to plugin or ClawHub options if maintainers decide core should not own smart/custom exclusion policy.

recommendation.title: Review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, live proof, protected-path semantics, and restore-critical defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the current backup volatile-filter retry fix and is the clearest current routing signal for backup reliability decisions.
